summary:
The headline signal today isn't a hot 14-day cell — it's the complete absence of one. Every rating shows 0-0 across trends, runs, sp, bullpen, hitting, and bullpen_fatigue in the 14-day window, meaning this late-season slate has been thin and the model's recent-form read is essentially frozen. What is live and worth trusting is the streak data: all four ratings (R1-R4) are riding a 3-game winning streak on starting pitcher (sp) picks, while all four are simultaneously stuck in a 3-game losing streak on bullpen_fatigue. That split is the swing factor for today — any matchup where sp and bullpen_fatigue point in opposite directions should default to the sp signal, and bullpen_fatigue-driven picks need to be faded or at minimum downgraded in confidence until that streak breaks.

On the board today, lean hardest into games where trends+sp or trends+runs both agree — those combos sit atop the season leaderboard at 58.0% (370-268, n=638) and 57.3% (404-301, n=705) respectively, and with 14-day data dark, these multi-category agreements are the most reliable filter available. Cross-reference team trends: MIL (51-23, 69%, n=74) and TBR (44-19, 70%, n=63) remain the model's best friends when picked, and both carry strong-play marks north of +18 units, so any slate appearance from either team with a trends+sp agreement is a green light. BOS (70%, n=56, strong 76%/+19.0u) and LAD (70%, n=56, strong 80%/+27.0u) are right behind them and should be treated as auto-plays when the model likes them straight up. Conversely, NYY remains the one team to handle carefully — 49% overall and a losing strong-play record (39%, -4.0u) — so any NYY lean today needs extra category agreement before trusting it, especially given the current bullpen_fatigue cold streak that could be dragging a NYY-involved pick down further. With sample sizes thin across the board, stack categories rather than trust any single rating in isolation today.
